A flying start to a life of learning…
Welcome to Gastrells Primary School
Welcome from the Headteacher – Mrs Helen Seward
Gastrells Primary School has a proud history and an exciting future. We are a welcoming school where children feel valued, safe and inspired to succeed.
Our approach is guided by our PRIDE values. We promote Positivity, encouraging confidence, enthusiasm and a love of learning. Respect is central to our community, helping everyone care for themselves, others and the environment. We celebrate Inclusivity, ensuring every child feels they belong and has equal opportunities to thrive.
Through Determination and Challenge, we support children to build resilience and a growth mindset. Above all, we strive for Excellence, helping every pupil achieve their best and grow into confident, compassionate individuals.
These values underpin all aspects of school life and create a supportive learning environment where children can succeed both academically and personally.
It’s friendly, they support you, they help everyone in different circumstances with different needs. They push you towards achieving your goals. It’s a fun school, you learn while having fun. The teachers are really fun. It’s a great place and friendly environment. They do lots of sport. I love it because it’s an amazing school and because of all the opportunities I’ve had and all the times I’ve pushed myself and achieved my goals.

pageCache.pageTitle: P.S.H.E and R.S.E Curriculum at Gastrells
pageCache.text:
(Personal, Social, Health, and Economic education) (Relationship and Sex Education)
At Gastrells, Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) are integral parts of our broad and balanced curriculum. Together, they support pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development and promote Citizenship and British Values.
Children are nurtured and supported to become healthy, confident and responsible members of society, with a strong understanding of tolerance, respect and diversity. Through PSHE and RSE, pupils learn to value themselves and others, celebrate inclusivity and develop positive relationships.
We encourage our children to become positive role models who are equipped with the knowledge, skills and attitudes needed to make informed choices and thrive both in school and beyond, supporting a strong foundation for lifelong learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care – Breakfast and Afterschool Club
pageCache.text:
At Gastrells Primary School, we’re proud to offer Wraparound Care through our well-established Breakfast and After School Clubs — providing a safe, happy, and nurturing environment for all children aged 4 to 11.
Our clubs are run by experienced, caring staff who ensure every child starts and ends their day feeling supported, engaged, and ready to learn.z
Bookings should be made and paid for in advance via School Money. For emergency or late bookings, please contact the school office to check availability.
Breakfast Club — Start the Day the Happy Way!
Our Gastrells Breakfast Club runs term time, Monday to Friday from 8:00am to 8:45am, giving children a calm, cheerful, and positive start to their school day.
A healthy breakfast is served daily — with a choice of cereals and toast — and children can enjoy relaxed, fun activities such as board games, puzzles, and quiet reading before lessons begin. We’re proud to have a 5* Food Hygiene Rating, ensuring every meal is both safe and delicious!
Children are supervised by our friendly staff throughout the session, and parents or guardians must sign them in each morning. At 8:45am, children are escorted to their classrooms ready for registration.
Cost: £5.50 per session, payable weekly or monthly in advance via School Money.There are usually a few spare places for last-minute bookings — please contact the school office to check availability.
After School Club — Relax, Play, and Unwind!
Our After School Club provides a safe, fun, and friendly space for children to relax and play after a busy day at school. Sessions run Monday to Friday during term time, with flexible timings to suit your family’s needs:
Children can enjoy a variety of activities — from games, puzzles, and arts & crafts to quiet reading or homework time. Those attending the full or later session receive a light meal, freshly prepared in line with our 5* Food Hygiene standards.
All sessions take place in the school hall, and children can be safely collected at the end of their session.
Bookings should be made and paid for in advance via School Money. For emergency or late bookings, please contact the school office to check availability.
How to Register and Book
Please use the links below to access the registration form, club rules, and booking information.
All sessions should be booked and paid for in advance through the School Money App. We aim to offer as much flexibility as possible — you can make bookings right up until midnight the night before a session. We’ll also do our best to accommodate last-minute bookings if space allows.
If you pay using Universal Credit, Tax Credits, or Childcare Vouchers, there’s a slightly different booking process. Please contact the school office for more information and guidance.

At Gastrells, we believe that music plays a vital role in developing pupils’ creativity, imagination and self-confidence, while also supporting their wellbeing. Music allows children to explore the world around them and express themselves in a variety of meaningful ways.
We follow the Charanga scheme to structure and plan our music curriculum, ensuring that knowledge and skills are taught progressively, building term by term and year by year as pupils move through the school.
Children at Gastrells benefit from a wide range of hands-on musical experiences. Pupils are given regular opportunities to perform, listen to and evaluate music through first-hand experiences. Every child takes part in a class performance, which includes a variety of musical elements, and all pupils perform in a Christmas carol concert and participate in weekly singing assemblies.
From Year 4 onwards, children also have the opportunity to perform as part of Young Voices, singing in a large-scale concert alongside pupils from other schools. In addition, pupils can access instrumental tuition including piano, violin, guitar, drumming and rock band sessions, alongside visiting workshops delivered by Make Music Gloucestershire.
Through these experiences, we aim to foster a lifelong enjoyment and appreciation of music while developing confidence, collaboration and performance skills.
We are very proud to be recognised as a Music Mark school. The Music Mark Award recognises the wide range of opportunities that are provided for children at Gastrells to share and enjoy music, to learn through music and to develop their musical understanding.

Computing Curriculum at Gastrells
At Gastrells, we want every child to become a confident, capable and responsible user of technology.
Our computing curriculum is engaging, creative and challenging, giving children opportunities to develop their skills in a range of areas while learning how to use technology safely and respectfully.
We recognise the important role technology plays in children’s lives. Through our computing curriculum, we prepare children with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to use technology effectively both in school and beyond.

It is our intention to secure the reading, writing and language skills children need to become enthusiastic and independent learners. We aim to provide all pupils with a sequential and carefully planned learning experience that equips them with the essential tools to succeed at Gastrells School and beyond.
We seek to immerse children in a rich range of high-quality texts to foster a love of reading, a passion for discovery and the confidence to explore the world through language. By placing literature at the heart of learning, we support children in developing curiosity, imagination and a lifelong appreciation of reading.
English underpins learning across the whole curriculum and is fundamental to both educational achievement and social development. Through exposure to a wide range of quality texts and meaningful discussion, we aim to support children in becoming thoughtful, engaged and contributing members of society.
The development of language skills is given high priority at Gastrells. We strive to nurture confident speakers, readers and writers who can communicate creatively and imaginatively, ensuring every child is supported to achieve their full potential in all aspects of English.

At Gastrells, our Geography curriculum encourages children to be curious about the world around them and to understand their place within it.
Starting with our local area and gradually exploring the wider world, children develop knowledge and understanding of places, people, cultures and environments.
Through engaging lessons and real-life experiences, children explore both the natural and human world, developing their understanding of how our planet works and how people interact with their environment.
We aim to inspire a fascination with the world, encouraging children to ask questions, explore, investigate and appreciate the diverse and ever-changing world in which we live.

At Gastrells, our History curriculum helps children develop a strong understanding of the past and how it has shaped the world we live in today.
Children develop a secure chronological understanding of local, British and world history, while learning to ask questions, investigate evidence and think critically about the past.
Through engaging lessons, first-hand experiences and educational visits, children explore a wide range of historical periods, people and events. Our local area provides many opportunities to bring history to life, alongside visits further afield such as London and the Forest of Dean.
We aim to inspire children to be curious about the past, understand different perspectives and develop a lasting interest in history.

In P.E we aim to inspire all children at Gastrells and through our inclusive approach for each child to fulfil their potential through positive and motivating experiences. PE enables pupils to become physically confident and our intention is that all children who leave Gastrells are physically literate which ultimately supports their health, wellbeing and fitness and provides ‘a flying start to’ lifelong activity.​
Our curriculum aims to ensure that all pupils:​
​All children at Gastrells receive a minimum of 2 hours of P.E a week with specialist coaches or class teachers. We plan their sessions to cover a broad and full range of skills and activities. Children in Year 1 and Year 2 attend swimming lessons in a local pool and children in Y5 carry out Rookie Lifeguard training.​
In addition to this we offer the children wide range of physically active extra-curricular clubs which both before and after school and at lunch time.
